title: Quota-friendly Guided Wizard — PRD sketch
content:
Problem statement:
Many teams hit token/quota limits during integration or production spikes and respond by throttling or disabling features. Engineers want a lightweight, user-facing tool to guide developers/product managers to a version of an LLM-driven feature that preserves core user value while staying within strict quota or cost envelopes.

Goal (one-liner):
Create a guided wizard inside the Console + SDK that recommends and previews quota-friendly prompt/model configurations and UX fallbacks for a given integration, so teams can ship predictable experiences under tight cost constraints.

Primary user(s):
- Platform/product engineers who must ship an LLM feature under quota/cost constraints
- Developer leads evaluating trade-offs for self-serve customers
- Solutions engineers prepping enterprise POCs with strict token budgets

Key outcomes / success metrics (90 days):
- Average tokens per request reduction for wizard-assisted flows: target >=25%
- Time to create a quota-compliant configuration: < 15 minutes (console wizard flow)
- % of POCs that remain within budget after deploy (survey): +15pp vs baseline
- Net negative customer support tickets related to unexpected token overages: -30%

Core capabilities (MVP):
1) Quota estimator pane
   - Paste sample prompt(s) (or link to route) and sample conversational trace; estimator simulates token usage across model choices and sequence/caching settings.
   - Shows per-token cost, expected variance, and 90th/95th percentile token consumption given distribution of session lengths.

2) Guided prompt transformer
   - A set of heuristics and automated transforms (compression, slotting, outline-to-short, instruction trimming) with toggleable previews.
   - Live "tokens saved" estimate per transform.

3) Fidelity slider + model suggestion
   - Slider from "Max fidelity" to "Budget first" that maps to recommended model family (e.g., rw-std -> rw-compact -> gated-quantized) plus quantization profile suggestions.
   - Includes fallback rules: substitute model variants on quota breach, fallback response templates for worst-case.

4) Preview + A/B pack
   - Side-by-side preview: original prompt vs transformed prompt output (sampled via sandboxed calls).
   - Allow quick A/B test config that routes 5/95 or similar to test production impacts.

5) Export / SDK snippet
   - Generates a ready-to-run SDK snippet with the chosen model, batching, prefix-caching hints, and rollout policy (canary % + fallback).

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I can paste a conversational transcript and see recommended prompt compressions that keep the assistant useful while trimming token cost, so I can hit a $500/month quota.
- As a solutions engineer, I can get a console-generated config that pins a compact model with an inline fallback template I can hand to a customer for compliance review.
- As an SRE, I can export a rollout policy that automatically downgrades to a cheaper model on quota alert and falls back to cached recaps for heavy sessions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: wizard runs with sample input and produces transform suggestions; preview uses sandboxed hosted API (no billing to customer)
- SDK export is copy-pastable and contains middleware for measuring tokens and enforcing per-session budget caps
- Wizard provides at least 3 transform strategies and quantifies estimated tokens saved for each
- Logging: suggested config includes telemetry hooks for token telemetry accessible in Console Optimize dashboards

Implementation notes / possibilities:
- Leverage Redwood Optimize data to map model -> cost and model performance percentiles for typical prompt shapes.
- Use a lightweight local transformer (prompt-parsing heuristics) to avoid repeated LLM calls when computing token-savings estimates; fall back to sandbox calls for final preview.
- Integrate with existing rollout primitives (canary, A/B, fallback) already in Console/Console API.
- For previews, cap SANDBOX calls to 5 per preview and cache results for the same transform.

UX sketch (flow):
1) Start wizard -> paste prompt or attach route -> select "budget target" ($/month or tokens/month) or choose "quota" from billing account
2) Wizard runs estimator -> shows spine: baseline tokens, target tokens, gap
3) Recommend a set of transforms with sliders and inline previews; user toggles to accept one or combine multiple
4) Choose fidelity slider -> wizard picks model family and quantization profile -> preview updated
5) Export config or deploy A/B pack with rollout policy

Edge cases & constraints:
- For multimodal or instruction-heavy prompts, estimator variance is high; surface confidence bands and suggest conservative profiles.
- Admins may want to override model substitutions for compliance—need to support allowlist/denylist of models per account.
- Offline/private deployments: wizard should output recommendations but not call hosted sandbox; use local cost table and encourage customer to run internal validation.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How accurate do we need estimator percentiles to be before shipping? (10% error vs 30% error acceptance)
- Should transforms be reversible (store original + transform) and to what degree do we provide audit trails for transform changes?
- Billing model: preview sandbox calls should not consume customer credits; will require internal metering.

Rough roadmap (6–12 weeks):
- Week 1–2: Specs + UI wireframes + cost model mapping (Redwood Optimize)
- Week 3–4: Estimator backend + simple transform rules (compression, instruction trim)
- Week 5–7: Sandbox preview + model mapping + export generation
- Week 8–10: Integrate rollout primitives + telemetry + QA on accuracy bands
- Week 11–12: Beta with 5 internal teams, iterate on UX and transforms

Next steps / owners:
- Product: Mira (owner) — finalize PRD, wireframes, acceptance criteria by 2026-03-01
- Eng (Mika Sato) — prototype estimator and transform engine, PoC sandbox integration
- Applied ML (Devon Patel) — supply model performance/cost mapping and fidelity thresholds
- Solutions (Ravi Menon) — pick 2 POCs to try wizard in beta

Notes to self (brainstorm bits):
- Could offer an "auto-mode" that picks a minimal set of transforms to hit target tokens with one click; show change log for transparency.
- Consider a "continuous monitor" option: after deploy, Console flags routes trending above budget and suggests transform rollouts automatically.
- Nice-to-have: token-level heatmap that highlights which parts of the prompt cost the most (system vs user vs context) to guide targeted trimming.
